stem: Johnny is now intubated, sedated and ventilated in the resus room. Which of the following aspects of his physiology should be monitored to limit the development of secondary brain injury?
explanation: In severe head injury, prevention of secondary brain injury focuses on avoiding hypotension, hypoxia, hypercapnia/hypocapnia, fever, and hypoglycaemia. Of the listed options, blood pressure is the best single answer because maintaining adequate perfusion is a core priority and hypotension is a major avoidable cause of secondary brain injury.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury

rationale: Selected existing option because the item can be preserved as a single-best-answer question with one clearly best option.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Blood pressure should be closely monitored and maintained to avoid hypotension and preserve cerebral perfusion.
optionExplanations.B: Important supportive care, but it is not the best answer to the question about physiology to monitor.
optionExplanations.C: Electrolytes may matter, but sodium is not the key single physiology parameter here.
optionExplanations.D: CO2 must be monitored in ventilated head injury, but blood pressure is the best single answer among these options.
optionExplanations.E: Oxygenation is essential, but the question asks for one best monitored aspect; blood pressure is the most directly prioritised option here.
optionExplanations.F: Temperature should be monitored to avoid fever, but it is not the best single answer in this set.
optionExplanations.G: Blood glucose should be monitored to avoid hypoglycaemia, but it is not the best single answer in this set.
optionExplanations.H: Too broad for a single-best-answer question and therefore not correct.

Clinical scenario 1 - Johnny

Teaching/Learning points:

Rapid neurological assessment

GCS including AVPU and Modified GCS

Prevention of secondary insult

Johnny is a 10 year old boy. He is en-route to the emergency department via ambulance following a fall from his bike. Paramedics have called ahead, stating Johnny was riding downhill and hit the side of a parked car at the bottom. He was thrown over the car, landing on the street. He was not wearing a helmet and was apparently knocked unconscious.

He is described as semi-conscious, breathing at a rate of 18/min, sats 98% in air, heart rate 90pbm. He has a large swelling to the right side of his head, and no other obvious injuries. Their ETA is 15 minutes.

The following ten questions refer to Johnny’s clinical scenario.
